model_priors.model_reasoning: This is a type II single-pass membrane protein: N-terminus cytoplasmic (~65 aa), single TM helix, and a large ~674 aa extracellular C-terminal ectodomain. Endocytic sorting motifs can only function in the ~65-residue cytoplasmic N-terminal segment (approximately residues 1-65: MMDQARSAFSNLFGGEPLSYTRFSLARQVDGDNSHVEMKLAVDEEENADNNTKANVTKPKRCSGS). Scanning this cytoplasmic region: there is a tyrosine at position ~21 (Y in ...SLARQ / ...TRFSLA context) — checking YxxΦ: 'YTRF' at ~Y20-T-R-F gives a Y-x-x-Φ (F is hydrophobic) tyrosine-based motif, which is a canonical internalization signal. There is no clear NPXY or [DE]XXXL[LI] dileucine motif visible in the cytoplasmic stretch (the acidic run DEEENADNN lacks the LL/LI dileucine). The presence of a plausible YxxΦ-type tyrosine motif in the cytoplasmic tail provides positive evidence for clathrin-mediated internalization, but a single motif with a large ectodomain and modest tail argues for partial rather than wholesale surface clearance. I therefore grade this as a genuine middle case (moderate). I am not identifying the protein and reason only from sequence/topology; confidence is moderate given one plausible motif but no corroborating dileucine/NPXY.

per_isoform.topology_summary: Type II single-pass: cytoplasmic N-terminus (~65 aa), 1 TM helix, large extracellular C-terminal ectodomain (~674 aa).
per_isoform.endocytic_motifs_noted: Cytoplasmic N-terminal tail (~res 1-65) contains a plausible tyrosine-based YxxΦ motif (Y-T-R-F, ~res 20-23); no clear NPXY or [DE]XXXL[LI] dileucine motif detected in the cytoplasmic region.
per_isoform.rationale: The only cytoplasmically exposed region is the ~65-aa N-terminal tail, the sole place sorting signals can act. It carries a candidate YxxΦ tyrosine motif capable of recruiting clathrin adaptors, providing positive sequence evidence for internalization. However, the motif is singular, the tail is short, and the bulk of the protein is a large ectodomain, so complete/rapid surface clearance is not strongly implied. This is a genuine intermediate case: internalization likely occurs but a substantial surface pool would plausibly persist, warranting a moderate grade with moderate confidence.

basal.rationale: Multiple independent sources confirm constitutive, clathrin-mediated endocytosis of TfR1 in the absence of added exogenous therapeutic binders. Reticulocyte studies show 2.5-fold uptake over surface binding saturating at 20-30 min; BBB endothelial cells show constitutive internalization of transferrin-bound iron; astrocyte studies confirm clathrin-mediated basal endocytosis. The receptor is described as one of the most dynamic and active membrane transport processes.

native_ligand.rationale: Transferrin (holo-Tf) binding to TfR1 drives robust clathrin-mediated endocytosis, described as one of the most dynamic and active membrane transport processes. Uptake at 37°C exceeded surface binding at 4°C by 2.5-fold and saturated after 20-30 min in reticulocytes. Transferrin-derived nanoparticles and Tf-conjugated complexes also confirm efficient TfR1-mediated uptake via clathrin-coated pits in multiple cell lines.

therapeutic.rationale: Multiple therapeutic binders directed at TfR1 show efficient internalization: anti-TfR1 antibody T8IgG1 undergoes efficient TfR1-mediated internalization on tumor cells; ch128.1Av IgG3-avidin fusion delivers biotinylated agents via receptor-mediated endocytosis; KB-tag engages TFRC at lysine 193 for clathrin-mediated uptake; CD71-targeted micelles and ASO-antibody conjugates exploit TfR1 for CNS delivery via transcytosis. Anti-TfR1 antibodies also drive transcytosis across the BBB.

literature.rationale: TFRC/TfR1/CD71 is one of the best-characterized endocytic receptors in cell biology. All three modes (basal, native ligand, therapeutic) show high internalization supported by extensive, convergent evidence across multiple cell types, assay formats, and species. The receptor constitutively cycles via clathrin-mediated endocytosis, is dramatically upregulated on tumor cells, and is exploited by numerous therapeutic platforms including antibodies, ADCs, nanoparticles, and ASO conjugates for targeted delivery.
literature.cross_condition_note: Basal and native-ligand (transferrin) internalization are both high and mechanistically identical (clathrin-mediated), with the receptor recycling rapidly to the surface. Therapeutic binders (antibodies, engineered ligands) also achieve high internalization, but affinity and valency modulate the balance between recycling/transcytosis and lysosomal degradation—high-affinity bivalent antibodies can shift fate toward degradation, while lower-affinity or monovalent formats favor transcytosis across the BBB.
literature.trafficking_summary: After clathrin-mediated endocytosis, TfR1 traffics through early endosomes (Rab5-positive) to recycling endosomes and is predominantly recycled back to the plasma membrane; iron is released in acidic endosomes. Therapeutic antibodies with high affinity can redirect TfR1 toward lysosomal degradation rather than recycling. In mesangial cells, TfR1 can also route cargo to lysosomes.

source.title: Receptor-mediated endocytosis of transferrin and recycling of the transferrin receptor in rat reticulocytes

spans.quote: At 4 degrees C transferrin bound to receptors on the reticulocyte plasma membrane, and at 37 degrees C receptor-mediated endocytosis of transferrin occurred. Uptake at 37 degrees C exceeded binding at 4 degrees C by 2.5-fold and saturated after 20-30 min. During uptake at 37 degrees C, bound transferrin was internalized into a trypsin-resistant space. Trypsinization at 4 degrees C destroyed surface receptors, but with subsequent incubation at 37 degrees C, surface receptors rapidly appeared (albeit in reduced numbers), and uptake occurred at a decreased level.

sources.claim: After endocytosis, colloidal gold-transferrin (AuTf) clustered in coated pits and appeared in intracellular membrane-bounded compartments (small vesicles/tubules at 5-10 min, multivesicular endosomes at 20-35 min), which fused with the plasma membrane and released contents by exocytosis, demonstrating clathrin-mediated internalization and recycling of TfR.

source.title: Receptor-mediated endocytosis of transferrin and recycling of the transferrin receptor in rat reticulocytes

spans.quote: After endocytosis, transferrin was released, apparently intact, into the extracellular space. At 37 degrees C colloidal gold-transferrin (AuTf) clustered in coated pits and then appeared inside various intracellular membrane-bounded compartments. Small vesicles and tubules were labeled after short (5-10 min) incubations at 37 degrees C. Larger multivesicular endosomes became heavily labeled after longer (20-35 min) incubations. Multivesicular endosomes apparently fused with the plasma membrane and released their contents by exocytosis.

source.title: Targeting Transferrin Receptor 1 for Enhancing Drug Delivery Through the Blood-Brain Barrier for Alzheimer's Disease

spans.quote: Drug delivery to the brain faces a critical obstacle in the form of the blood-brain barrier (BBB), which severely limits therapeutic options for Alzheimer's disease (AD). Transferrin receptor 1 (TfR1) is abundantly expressed in brain capillary endothelial cells, offering a potential pathway for circumventing this barrier. Physiologically, TfR1 binds to iron-laden transferrin, leading to cellular uptake through clathrin-mediated endocytosis. Within acidic endosomes, the iron is released, and the receptor-apotransferrin complex recycles to the cell surface for further rounds of transport.
